# FDG5024

> DO use a property, rather than a method, if the value of the property is stored in the process memory and the property would just provide access to the value.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 5.1.3 Choosing Between Properties and Methods.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1024
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library suggestion, application suggestion, test none
- Status: draft

CA1024 reports an externally visible parameterless method whose name starts with Get and that returns a value. It does not see whether the value is stored in memory; a Get method that computes, allocates or has side effects should stay a method (FDG5025). CA1024 has no code fix, and turning a method into a property changes the public API. A suggestion: in the noise samples 1 of 5 reports was a method that gathers system information, which FDG5025 keeps a method.

## From the book

For example, a member that retrieves the name of a `Customer` from a field stored in the object should be a property.

```csharp
public Customer {
  public Customer(string name){
    this.name = name;
  }
   public string Name {
    get { return this.name; }
  }
  private string name;
}
```
